SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Tertiary consumers

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Ice melting to water

2. A — 100 °C

3. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

6. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

7. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. A — Glucose and oxygen

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

10. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. C — Producers

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Change of State; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Levers as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
